The Yamamoto-first pass found no new unrecorded verified Tsuyoshi Yamamoto date. Michael Mayo clears RADAR admission because his use of the voice as an improvising instrument—multilayered harmony, rhythmic vocal language and beatboxing—creates a specific instrumental identity beyond a conventional vocal-jazz booking, and the October COTTON CLUB engagement presents that language with a compact current quartet. A+ captures the recommendation: this is an unusually strong contemporary performance worth actively making room for, while three nights and six sets provide enough access that the engagement does not require S-level scarcity.

events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents Michael Mayo on October 13–15, 2026, with two sets each night at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The announced quartet is Michael Mayo on voice, Andrew Freedman on keyboards, Kyle Miles on bass, and Robin Baytas on drums. The venue describes Mayo's approach as using the voice like an instrument, including multilayered chorus and beatboxing, and notes his two nominations at the 68th Grammy Awards for Best Jazz Performance and Best Jazz Vocal Album. The engagement marks his return to COTTON CLUB roughly a year and a half after his previous appearance there. Web reservations have been open since August 1, 2026.

en.why_it_matters: Mayo is interesting here because the voice is not just carrying songs; it is doing jobs normally split among horn, rhythm section and studio arrangement. Layered harmony, rhythmic syllables and beatboxing sit inside a live quartet with enough space for the vocal line to function as an improvising instrument. That gives this engagement a specific contemporary identity rather than making it another strong singer passing through a Tokyo jazz club.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the six sets if October overlaps with Tokyo, especially if contemporary improvisation and unusual instrumental language are part of the trip. Three nights provide enough flexibility that a genuinely singular master appearance or one-off elsewhere in Kanto would still take precedence.

es.why_it_matters: Lo interesante aquí es que Mayo no usa la voz sólo para cantar canciones: la pone a hacer trabajos que normalmente se reparten entre un instrumento melódico, la sección rítmica y el arreglo de estudio. Capas de armonía, sílabas rítmicas y beatboxing viven dentro de un cuarteto con suficiente espacio para que la voz funcione realmente como instrumento de improvisación. Eso le da a estas noches una identidad contemporánea muy concreta, más allá de ser simplemente otro gran vocalista pasando por un club de jazz en Tokio.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a uno de los seis sets si octubre coincide con Tokio, sobre todo si la improvisación contemporánea y los lenguajes instrumentales poco convencionales forman parte del viaje. Tres noches dan suficiente flexibilidad para que un maestro en un contexto verdaderamente singular o un one-off raro en otro punto de Kanto todavía tenga precedencia.
